title: Into the market
hook: picture ten: the herder walks into town with open hands, helping (Ox-Herding 10)
tomorrow: who did Marcus Aurelius thank first in his notebook?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the river flows: the plain world handed back, just as it is. One picture left, and an argument to go with it.

Some days the dream is a cabin with no signal. Other days it's being right in the thick of things, useful. Zen has heroes on both sides. On one, Hanshan, the poet of Cold Mountain, whose poems describe a life up among the cliffs, far from any road. On the other, Kuoan's tenth picture: the herder walking into the market, chest bare, feet bare, grinning, with open hands. Two heroes, two directions. Which one is the end of the path?
screen: `A CABIN, OR THE THICK OF IT?` → `HANSHAN ON COLD MOUNTAIN.` → `THE HERDER IN THE MARKET.`

segments.voice: Let the hermit speak first. Hanshan's poems say no road reaches Cold Mountain; up there, among clouds and pines, the world's noise can't touch the mind. Their best case: you can't give what you haven't found, and finding takes quiet. A guide who has never been alone with their own mind has little to hand anyone. And tradition says even Hanshan came down now and then, to a temple kitchen, where his friend Shide saved him the leftovers. Now the market. The preface says the herder's gate is shut, and even the wise don't know his inner life. He carries a gourd of wine into the market and leans on his staff on the way home. In the wine shop and the fish market, everyone he meets wakes up. The verse: dusty, smeared with ash, smiling wide, no need for the powers of the gods; he simply makes dead trees bloom. Their best case: the whole series was for this. Awakening that stays on the mountain hasn't finished the circle. Zen honors both. But Kuoan's ten pictures end in town. The title of the last one says it: entering the market with open hands.
screen: `THE HERMIT: FINDING TAKES QUIET.` · `EVEN HANSHAN CAME TO THE KITCHEN.` · `THE MARKET: DEAD TREES BLOOM.` · `THE PICTURES END IN TOWN.` · then, large: `OPEN HANDS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person in your town who could use a hand this week: a neighbor with groceries, a coworker, someone at the shop. Picture the help itself, then the thing most likely to stop you, then what you'll do when that thing shows up.
Into the market: Kuoan's tenth picture. Back in town, dusty and smiling, helping with open hands.
Hold onto this: open hands, because the pictures end in the market, not on the mountain. All ten, done.

screen: `DAY 1788 COUNTS.` → `OX-HERDING · PICTURE 10 OF 10.` → `THE SUMMIT · 12 OF 15.` → `TOMORROW: WHO DID MARCUS AURELIUS THANK FIRST?`

howItsDone: Zen honors both the hermit, like Hanshan, and the teacher who returns to ordinary life; the tenth ox-herding picture shows a smiling figure in the market. People on this path bring their practice back into town as help.

Hanshan.meaning: a Chinese hermit poet; his name means Cold Mountain

Shide.meaning: Hanshan's friend in tradition, a temple kitchen worker

Kuoan.meaning: the Chinese Zen teacher behind the ten ox-herding verses

Zen.meaning: a school of Buddhism centered on sitting and direct seeing
